schema.description:
A stream of Server-Sent Events. Parse it per the [SSE Streaming guide](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/guides/streaming): read `data:` lines, dispatch on the `event` field, skip `ping` (keep-alive; a Chatflow stream opens with one, then more arrive roughly every 10 seconds).

**Events by app type** (the reply events, then how the stream closes):

- **Chatbot**: `message` chunks (concatenate in order) → `message_end`.
- **Agent**: `agent_thought` reasoning and tool-call steps alongside `agent_message` chunks → `message_end`.
- **New Agent**: `agent_message` chunks with `agent_thought` steps alongside → one closing `message` carrying the complete answer (treat it as the final answer, not extra text to append) → `message_end`. Its `message_end` metadata carries `usage` (plus `annotation_reply` on an annotation match) and never `retriever_resources`.
- **Chatflow**: `workflow_started` → node events (`node_started`, `node_finished`, plus iteration and loop variants) alongside `message` chunks → then, by outcome:
  - **Success**: `message_end`, then `workflow_finished`
  - **Failure**: `workflow_finished` with status `failed`, then `error`; no `message_end`
  - **Pause**: `human_input_required`, then `workflow_paused` (the stream ends here; the run resumes separately)

**Add-ons**:

- Text-to-speech auto-play: `tts_message` audio chunks interleave, and `tts_message_end` trails the closing event.
- Chatflow LLM nodes with `reasoning_format: separated` also emit `reasoning_chunk` deltas carrying the model's reasoning.

**Common fields**: apart from `ping`, every event includes `conversation_id`, `message_id`, and `created_at` (Unix epoch seconds); all but `error` also include `task_id`. Workflow, node, and human-input events (Chatflow apps) nest their payload under `data` and, except for `agent_log`, carry a top-level `workflow_run_id`.

**Reply events**

| Event | App | Fires on | Key fields |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `message` | Chatbot, Chatflow, New Agent | each answer chunk (concatenate in order); for New Agent, one closing chunk with the complete answer | `answer` |
| `agent_message` | Agent, New Agent | each answer chunk (concatenate in order) | `answer` |
| `agent_thought` | Agent, New Agent | each reasoning or tool-call step | `position`, `thought`, `tool`, `tool_input` (JSON), `observation`, `message_files` |
| `message_replace` | All | output moderation replaces the answer so far | `answer`; Chatflow also `reason` |
| `reasoning_chunk` | Chatflow | each reasoning-content delta, when an LLM node uses `reasoning_format: separated` (concatenate in order; a final `is_final: true` event marks reasoning finished and may carry an empty `reasoning`) | `data.message_id`, `data.reasoning`, `data.node_id`, `data.is_final` |
| `message_file` | Chatbot, Agent | the assistant returns a file | `type`, `belongs_to`, `url` |
| `message_end` | All | the answer is complete | `metadata` (`usage`, `retriever_resources`) |
| `tts_message`, `tts_message_end` | Chatbot, Agent, Chatflow | audio chunk / end, when TTS auto-play is on | `audio` |

**Workflow and node events** (Chatflow apps only)

Each event nests its payload under a `data` object.

| Event | Fires on | Key `data` fields |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `workflow_started` | the run begins | `inputs` |
| `node_started` | a node begins | `node_id`, `node_type`, `title` |
| `node_finished` | a node ends | `status`, `outputs`, `execution_metadata` |
| `node_retry` | a node retries after a failure | `retry_index` |
| `iteration_started`, `iteration_next`, `iteration_completed` | Iteration node progress (informational) | `data` |
| `loop_started`, `loop_next`, `loop_completed` | Loop node progress (informational) | `data` |
| `agent_log` | an Agent node step log (informational; no `workflow_run_id`) | `data` |
| `workflow_finished` | the run ends | `status` (`succeeded`, `failed`, `partial-succeeded`, `stopped`), `outputs`, `total_tokens` |
| `workflow_paused` | the run pauses | `paused_nodes`, `reasons` |
| `human_input_required` | the run reaches a Human Input node | `form_token`, `form_content`, `expiration_time` |

After a pause this stream ends at `workflow_paused`. Submit the form via [Submit Human Input Form](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/human-input/submit-human-input-form) or let it time out; the resumed run, including `human_input_form_filled`/`human_input_form_timeout` through `workflow_finished`, streams from [Stream Workflow Events](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/workflow-runs/stream-workflow-events).

**Transport events**

| Event | Fires on | Key fields |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `error` | a failure ends the stream; HTTP stays `200` | `status` (e.g. `400`), `code` (e.g. `invalid_param`), `message` |
| `ping` | keep-alive; opens every Chatflow stream, then roughly every 10 seconds | none |

post.description:
**Available for**: Chatflow, Workflow, New Agent, Chatbot, Agent, Text Generator apps.

Uploads a file and returns its `id` for later requests to reference. The file belongs to the uploading end user: only requests carrying the same `user` can reference it.

Which file types an app actually consumes depends on its file-upload settings; read them from [Get App Parameters](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/applications/get-app-parameters).

file.description:
The file to upload, as one `multipart/form-data` part. The filename must not contain `/` or `\`.

Any extension is accepted unless it is on the deployment's security blacklist (`UPLOAD_FILE_EXTENSION_BLACKLIST`, empty by default).

Size limits per category: images 10 MB, audio 50 MB, video 100 MB, other files 15 MB by default (Dify Cloud uses the defaults). Self-hosted deployments adjust them with the `UPLOAD_*_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT` [environment variables](/en/self-host/deploy/configuration/environments).

user.description: End-user identifier this upload belongs to, defined by your app and unique within it. Omit it to attribute the upload to the shared `DEFAULT-USER`. Only later requests with the same `user` can reference the file. See [End User Identity](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/guides/end-user-identity).

- `no_file_uploaded` : No file was provided in the request.
- `too_many_files` : Only one file is allowed per request.
- `filename_not_exists_error` : The uploaded file has no filename.
- `invalid_param` : The filename contains `/` or `\`, or the file's extension is on the deployment's blacklist.

200.description:
Successful response. The content type and structure depend on the `response_mode` parameter in the request.

- If `response_mode` is `blocking`, returns `application/json` with a `WorkflowBlockingResponse` object.
- If `response_mode` is `streaming`, returns `text/event-stream` with a stream of `ChunkWorkflowEvent` objects.

schema.description:
A stream of Server-Sent Events. Parse it per the [SSE Streaming guide](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/guides/streaming): read `data:` lines, dispatch on the `event` field, skip `ping` (keep-alive; the stream opens with one, then more arrive roughly every 10 seconds).

**Stream lifecycle**: The stream closes when a `workflow_finished`, `workflow_paused`, or `error` event is received. Errors are delivered in-stream with HTTP status `200`; inspect the event payload for details rather than relying on the status code.

**Reasoning events**:
- `reasoning_chunk`: A chain-of-thought delta from an LLM node whose `reasoning_format` is `separated`. Concatenate consecutive `reasoning_chunk` events to rebuild the full reasoning; an event with `is_final: true` marks the node finished thinking (and may carry an empty `reasoning`). The payload sits under `data` and, unlike chat apps, carries `message_id: null` and no `conversation_id`. The parallel `text_chunk` stream stays free of `<think>` tags.

**Human Input events**:
- `human_input_required`: Fires together with `workflow_paused` when the workflow reaches a Human Input node. Use the `form_token` from the payload to drive the form-handling flow via the [Human Input API](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/human-input/get-human-input-form).
- `human_input_form_filled`: A recipient submitted the form; workflow execution resumes.
- `human_input_form_timeout`: The form expired without a response. Workflow follows the timeout fallback edge if defined.

Runs the query that [Create Query Token](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/queries/create-query-token) issued a token for and streams the answer as Server-Sent Events. The credential is the query token, not the knowledge base API key. For the two-call flow and how to read the stream, see [Query the Knowledge Base](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/guides/knowledge-base#query-the-knowledge-base).

For which errors to retry and what the error details mean, see [Handle Errors](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/guides/knowledge-base#handle-errors).

Every call creates a query record. Repeating a call runs the query again and creates another record.

schema.description:
Each frame is an `event:` line naming the event plus a `data:` line holding one JSON object, with no `ping` keep-alive. Parse it per [Parse the Stream](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/guides/streaming#parse-the-stream) and dispatch on the `event:` line, because the JSON carries no `event` field.

**Events**

- `answer.delta`: one piece of the answer.
  - `delta`: the text to append.
  - `traceId`: the query record ID.
- `answer.done`: the answer is complete and its query record is saved.
  - `finishReason`: `retrieval-evidence` when chunks were found, `no-retrieval-evidence` when nothing matched.
  - `metadata`: carries `mode` and `evidenceBundle` at `fast`, `deep`, and `research` depth, `citations` with `retrieval-evidence`, and other keys the run produced.
  - `traceId`: the query record ID.
- `answer.error`: the query failed after the stream opened.
  - `code`: the failure, one of:
    - `RETRIEVAL_EXECUTION_LEASE_LOST`: the knowledge base entered deletion, or the run expired. Run the query again.
    - `KNOWLEDGE_FS_UNAVAILABLE`: any other failure while generating the answer or saving the query record.
  - `error`: the message.
  - `failure`: error details: `category`, `code`, `message`, `retryPolicy`, `stage`, `traceId`, and optionally `action`.
    - `stage`: always `query_generation`.
  - `traceId`: the query record ID.

**`citations`**

One entry per retrieved chunk that supports the answer:

- `nodeId`: the chunk ID.
- `label`: `node:<nodeId>`.
- `documentAssetId`: the document file the chunk came from.
- `sectionPath`: the outline path.
- `pageNumber`
- `projectionIds`
- `sources`: which searches found the chunk: `dense`, `fts`, `pageindex`, or `visual`.

**Closing sequence by outcome**

- Success: zero or more `answer.delta`, then one `answer.done`, then the stream closes.
- Failure: `answer.error` in place of `answer.done`, then the stream closes. Pieces already delivered may precede it, and the HTTP status stays `200`. Treat it as final and start a new query to try again.
- Client disconnect. The run is canceled and the stream ends.

**Answer content**: at `fast` and `deep`, one `answer.delta` carries a digest of the retrieved chunks (`Retrieval evidence answer:` followed by numbered section paths and their text). At `research`, the synthesized answer streams as several pieces. When nothing matched, the single piece is `I could not find evidence for that query in the indexed retrieval projections.` and `finishReason` is `no-retrieval-evidence`. Answers are capped at 2,000 characters at every depth.

A successful run:

```text
event: answer.delta
data: {"delta":"Retrieval evidence answer:\n1. Policies / Refunds: Refund window extended from 14 to 30 days for annual plans.","traceId":"6c1f0b2e-9d3a-4f5b-8c7d-0e1f2a3b4c5d"}

event: answer.done
data: {"finishReason":"retrieval-evidence","metadata":{"mode":"fast","generator":"hybrid-query","topScore":0.83,"citations":[{"documentAssetId":"b3f4c8d2-6a1e-4f7b-9c0d-2e3f4a5b6c7d","label":"node:9f2e6b41-7c3d-4a58-b0e9-1d2c3f4a5b6e","nodeId":"9f2e6b41-7c3d-4a58-b0e9-1d2c3f4a5b6e","pageNumber":4,"projectionIds":["c7a0d5b2-3e14-4f89-a6b7-0c1d2e3f4a5b"],"sectionPath":["Policies","Refunds"],"sources":["dense","fts"]}],"evidenceBundle":{"createdAt":"2026-09-06T08:31:12Z","id":"e4b2f7a0-1c3d-4e58-9f6a-0b1c2d3e4f5a","items":[{"citations":[{"documentAssetId":"b3f4c8d2-6a1e-4f7b-9c0d-2e3f4a5b6c7d","documentVersion":3,"pageNumber":4,"sectionPath":["Policies","Refunds"]}],"conflicts":[],"freshness":{"status":"fresh"},"metadata":{},"nodeId":"9f2e6b41-7c3d-4a58-b0e9-1d2c3f4a5b6e","score":0.83,"scores":{"final":0.83,"retrieval":0.71},"text":"Refund window extended from 14 to 30 days for annual plans."}],"missingEvidence":[],"query":"What changed in the refund policy this quarter?","state":"answerable","traceId":"6c1f0b2e-9d3a-4f5b-8c7d-0e1f2a3b4c5d"}},"traceId":"6c1f0b2e-9d3a-4f5b-8c7d-0e1f2a3b4c5d"}
```

Items that Re-index Documents reported as `not_found` count as completed, so `completed_items` can equal `total_items` even when no document was re-indexed. For the metadata, deletion, and re-index flows, see [Maintain Documents](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/guides/knowledge-base#maintain-documents).

patch.description:
Updates a source's name, status, URI, metadata, or provider parameters, and can start a sync when the configuration changed.

Send at least one of `name`, `status`, `uri`, `metadata`, or `providerParameters`; `expectedVersion` and `syncAfterUpdate` alone are rejected.

expectedVersion.description: The source's current `version` from [Get Source](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/sources/get-source). A mismatch answers 409 instead of overwriting a concurrent change. Omit it to let the last write win.

status.description: New status, stored as given. Set `active` or `disabled`; `error` and `syncing` are set by sync runs, not by callers. A `disabled` source never syncs, so set `active` before requesting a sync.

uri.description: New URI. For `web` sources it must be an HTTP or HTTPS URL without embedded credentials; `metadata.parameters.url` is updated to match.

metadata.description: Keys to merge into the stored metadata (nested objects merge, arrays are replaced). Must not contain `parameters` (use `providerParameters`) or credentials. `datasource`, `pluginId`, `provider`, `providerId`, and `providerKind` cannot change. `tenantId` is overwritten by the service.

providerParameters.description: Plugin-specific options, replacing `metadata.parameters` as a whole. The keys are the data source plugin's own. Find them in the plugin's documentation. Values are booleans, finite numbers, or strings. Credential-like keys are rejected.

syncAfterUpdate.description: When `true`, starts a sync run after the write, but only if the update actually changed `uri`, `providerParameters`, or a metadata key other than `syncPolicy`, and the source is not `disabled`. Otherwise the flag has no effect and the response carries `sync_workflow: null`. Re-sending the current `uri` does not count as a change. When nothing needs changing, sync from the knowledge base's **Source** tab in Dify.

What is wrong with the setting:

- `missing`: the selection is absent, or rerank is disabled.
- `validation_failed`, `unavailable`, or `incompatible`: the pending settings failed validation; `incompatible` means a dimension or identity mismatch.
- `binding_missing`: the live models are not bound to the published content.
- `unavailable` on `publication`: the published content is not ready for every depth.

value.description: The cutoff score, 0 to 1. `null` when not set.

top_k.description: Maximum number of chunks a search returns, 1 to 100.

revision.description: Revision of the live retrieval settings. `null` while the settings are pending.

stage.description:
Pipeline stage. Forward order:

- `queued`
- `parsed`
- `outline_built`
- `nodes_generated`
- `projection_built`
- `smoke_eval_passed`
- `published`

`published` means the new revision is active. `failed` and `canceled` are the other terminal values. [Retry Indexing Task](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/indexing-tasks/retry-indexing-task) keeps the checkpoint the attempt had reached, so the value is rarely `queued` after a retry.

run_state.description:
Scheduler state of the current attempt:

- `dispatch_pending`: accepted, waiting to be dispatched to a worker.
- `queued`: dispatched, waiting for a worker.
- `running`: a worker is executing the task.
- `retry_wait`: an automatic retry is scheduled; `stage` stays unchanged.
- `succeeded`: accompanies `stage: published`.
- `failed`, `canceled`: terminal.
- `superseded`: a newer attempt replaced this one. Terminal, reported with `stage: canceled`, and accepted by neither cancel nor retry.

`null` when not set. [Retry Indexing Task](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/indexing-tasks/retry-indexing-task) sets it to `dispatch_pending`.

error.description: Short description of the failure. Set only when `stage` or `run_state` is `failed`; `null` otherwise, including on canceled tasks.

execution_attempts.description: Attempts made so far. Reset to `0` by [Retry Indexing Task](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/indexing-tasks/retry-indexing-task).

max_execution_attempts.description: Attempts allowed before the task fails.

base_head_revision.description: Internal. Not needed to follow the task.

candidate_fingerprint.description: Internal. Not needed to follow the task. `null` before the candidate exists.

candidate_publication_id.description: Internal. Not needed to follow the task. `null` before the candidate exists.

created_at.description: When the task was created, in epoch milliseconds.

updated_at.description: When the task last changed, in epoch milliseconds.

completed_at.description: When the task reached a terminal stage, in epoch milliseconds. `null` while it runs and after a retry.

data.description: Entries of this page, in the order the run recorded them.

name.description: Entry name. Chunks view: the chunk's node ID. Conflicts view: `conflict-<n>`, numbered from 1 within the chunk. Missing-chunks view: `missing-<n>`, numbered from 1.

path.description: Path of the entry inside the knowledge service. Informational. This API does not serve it.

resource_type.description: `node` in the chunks and conflicts views, `evidence` in the missing-chunks view.

target_id.description:
The entry's target:

- Chunks view: the chunk's node ID.
- Conflicts view: the chunk it conflicts with, or its own node ID when none is recorded.
- Missing-chunks view: the expected chunk ID when recorded, else the entry `name`.

May not resolve to a live chunk when `metadata.availability` is `unavailable`.

metadata.description: Details of the entry. Keys are camelCase and depend on the view. A key is present only when the view recorded it.

conflictCount.description: Chunks view: number of conflicts recorded on the chunk.

status.description: `fresh`, `stale`, or `unknown`.

score.description: Chunks view: relevance score of the chunk, from 0 to 1.

rerank.description: Rerank score. Present when a reranker ran.

text.description: Chunks view. Text of the chunk. A placeholder when the chunk is unavailable.

nodeId.description: Conflicts view: ID of the chunk that holds the conflict.

reason.description: Conflicts view. Free-text explanation of the conflict. Missing-chunks view. Why the chunk was not used, one of `not-retrieved`, `permission-filtered`, `stale`, `conflict`, or `unknown`. `permission-filtered` means the chunk exists but the key's scope excluded it.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or `null` on the last page. Send it back as `cursor`.

path.description: Path of the view inside the knowledge service, for example `/queries/<query_record_id>/evidence`. Informational. This API does not serve it.

truncated.description: `true` when more entries exist beyond this page.

code.description: Stable error code in upper snake case, for example `KNOWLEDGE_FS_CONFLICT` or `SOURCE_CREDENTIAL_TEST_FAILED`.

message.description: Fixed text for the `code` or, failing that, the `category`. Identical to the top-level `message`. Never the wording of a provider or of the knowledge service.

retryPolicy.description: Whether a retry can help: `automatic` (the service retries on its own), `manual` (retry yourself), `after_configuration` (fix the knowledge base's setup in Dify first), or `never` (change the request).

action.description: Suggested next step, when there is one: `configure_model`, `configure_parser`, `configure_source`, `contact_admin`, `reupload`, or `retry`. Absent otherwise.

stage.description: Stage the failure belongs to, for example `query_generation` or `credential-test`. Absent when not applicable.

traceId.description: Reference to quote when contacting an administrator. Always present on a `failure`.

parameters.description: Up to 8 values that qualify the failure, with keys among `attempt`, `documentCount`, `fileSizeBytes`, `limit`, `maxFileSizeBytes`, `maxItems`, `modelType`, `providerKind`, `retryAfterSeconds`, and `status`. Absent when there are none.

id.description: Research task ID. Use it as `research_task_id` in the task operations.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

budget_usd.description: Spend ceiling from the request in USD. `null` when none was set.

cost.description: Spend recorded so far. Keys are camelCase.

totalUsd.description: Sum of `entries[].costUsd` in USD. `0` until the first model call is recorded.

budgetUsd.description: The request's `budgetUsd`. Absent when no budget was set.

budgetExceeded.description: `true` when spend crossed `budgetUsd` and the task was canceled for that reason. Absent otherwise. This is the only way to tell a budget cancellation from [Cancel Research Task](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/research-tasks/cancel-research-task).

entries.description: One entry per recorded model call, oldest first.

costUsd.description: Cost of the call in USD.

provider.description: Model provider that served the call.

recordedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds when the cost was recorded.

step.description: Pipeline step that made the call, such as `plan` or `generate`.

usage.description: Token usage reported by the provider, such as `inputTokens` and `outputTokens`. Empty when the provider reported none.

limits.description: Limits from the request, with snake_case keys. `null` when the request carried no `limits`. A member that was not sent is `null`.

stage.description:
Where the task is in its lifecycle. Tasks move forward one stage at a time:

- `queued`: accepted, waiting for a worker.
- `planning`: resolving the retrieval plan.
- `retrieving`: searching the knowledge base. The retrieval checkpoint result is written when this stage ends.
- `analyzing`: reading and weighing the retrieved chunks.
- `generating`: writing the answer. The final result is written during this stage.
- `completed`: finished. The answer is in the last result of [List Research Task Results](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/research-tasks/list-research-task-results).
- `failed`: stopped with an error. See `error` and `failure`.
- `canceled`: stopped by [Cancel Research Task](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/research-tasks/cancel-research-task) or by the budget. See `cost.budgetExceeded`.
- `paused`: set aside by the server under load. Resumes on its own and can be canceled.

`completed`, `failed`, and `canceled` are terminal.

mode.description: Resolved retrieval depth: `fast`, `deep`, or `research`. A task created with `auto` stores the depth the reasoning model chose.

top_k.description: Number of chunks each search targets: the request's `topK`, or the knowledge base's **TOP K** when omitted.

metadata.description: The `metadata` object sent at creation, without keys that start with `__knowledgeFs`.

error.description: Failure code, the same value as `failure.code`. Present only when `stage` is `failed`; `null` otherwise, including for canceled tasks.

failure.description: Error details. Present only when `stage` is `failed`; `null` otherwise. Members without a value are `null` here. `traceId` is the task ID.

created_at.description: Epoch milliseconds when the task was created.

updated_at.description: Epoch milliseconds of the last change to `stage` or `cost`.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

- `completed` or `zero_results` run: `active`

metadata.description: Provider identity (`pluginId`, `provider`, `datasource`, `providerKind`, `credentialId`), provider parameters under `parameters`, and sync bookkeeping (`sync`, `crawled`, `imported`, `importedFiles`). Credential-like keys are removed before the response is sent.

permission_scope.description: IDs of the content scopes a reader's key must hold to see the source. Empty when every caller can see it.

connection_id.description: Connection the source uses for credentials. Pass it as `connectionId` when binding another source to the same connection. `null` when unbound.

credential_configured.description: `true` when the source holds a credential reference. `null` when the knowledge service does not report it.

version.description: Concurrency version, increased on every write. Send it as `expectedVersion` on [Update Source](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/sources/update-source) and as `expectedRevision` on [Delete Source](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/sources/delete-source).

last_synced_at.description: Completion time of the latest successful sync. Set by [List Sources](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/sources/list-sources) only; `null` elsewhere and when the source has never synced.

sync_policy.description: Sync schedule configured in Dify. Set by [List Sources](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/sources/list-sources) only; `null` elsewhere and when no schedule exists. Not writable over the API.

sync_workflow.description: Latest sync run. Set by [List Sources](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/sources/list-sources) when a run is active or newer than the source, and by [Update Source](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/sources/update-source) when the call started a sync. `null` otherwise. Watch its `state` to follow the run.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

mode.description: `manual` (no schedule), `interval` (the preset schedule chosen in Dify), or `custom` (every `custom_interval_seconds`).

custom_interval_seconds.description: Interval in seconds for `mode: custom`. `null` for the other modes.

next_run_at.description: When the next scheduled sync is due. `null` when nothing is scheduled.

revision.description: Policy revision. Increases on every change.

expected_source_version.description: Source `version` the policy was written against.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

kind.description: What the run does. A run started by [Update Source](/en/3.14.x/develop/api/sources/update-source) is `sync`; Dify-started runs are `crawl-preview`, `crawl-import`, `online-document-import`, `online-drive-import`, or `bulk`.

state.description:
Progress of the run.

Live states:

- `queued`: waiting for a worker
- `running`
- `crawling`: fetching website pages
- `preview_ready`: a crawl preview waiting for page selection in Dify
- `importing`: materializing documents
- `syncing`: refreshing existing documents

Terminal states:

- `completed`
- `zero_results`: nothing to import
- `failed`: see `failure`
- `canceled`

checkpoint.description: Last durable step the run reached. Used for resuming after a retry.

cursor.description: Provider cursor the run resumes from. `null` when the run has not paged.

max_execution_attempts.description: Attempts allowed before the run is marked `failed`.

progress_total.description: Items the run expects to process. `null` until known.

completed_at.description: When the run reached `completed` or `zero_results`. `null` before that.

canceled_at.description: When the run was canceled. `null` unless `state` is `canceled`.
